macro.headline: Bull regime intact but leadership rotating away from tech into cyclicals and healthcare.
macro.story:
The facts first: SPY sits at $744.78, up 1.4% on the week and 8.1% above its 200-day, with the market in a confirmed bull regime and drawdown only -1.9% from the 52-week high. But under the surface there's real tension — SPY's MACD histogram is negative (-0.23), QQQ is down 4.4% over 21 days with RSI at 48 and MACD bearish, while the Dow is running hot (RSI 70, +3.1% over 21 days) and the Russell 2000 is above its 50-day. VIX is quiet at 16.32, down 11% in five days, and the VIX3M/VIX curve is in healthy contango at 1.18. Breadth is constructive: 54% of the S&P is bullish, 9 of 11 GICS sectors are above their 50-day, and 78% of sector ETFs are participating. Commodities tell a different story — WTI oil is down 29% over 21 days with RSI at 28 (deeply oversold), gold and silver are in downtrends despite bouncing today, and DXY is grinding higher (+1.6% in 21 days, RSI 61).

The prevailing sentiment in the tracked conversation attributes the underlying bid to a record AI capex cycle — the dominant view frames roughly $850 billion in committed AI infrastructure spend from the mega-cap platforms as the structural driver, and points to the second-largest weekly inflow ever into US technology funds (~$14 billion) as confirmation. Sentiment leans firmly bullish on US equity dominance (framing the US as ~48% of global market cap at a record ~$81 trillion) and on Nasdaq 100 futures gapping up over 1% as markets reopened post-holiday. However, this sentiment narrative conflicts with the price data in one important way: the tracked voices are excited about mega-cap tech (MSFT, META, AMZN, MU, TSLA are heavily discussed), yet the Technology sector is BEARISH on our scoreboard (score 3.2, MACD bearish, RSI 47) and Nasdaq 100 is WEAK. The rotation is happening away from what sentiment is chasing — the narrative may be lagging the tape. A secondary bearish thread flags MicroStrategy's $216M bitcoin sale (BTC broke $62,000) and warns retail 0DTE options are a record 48% of retail volume — a positioning/speculation caution.

Rotationally, the leadership is in Utilities, Industrials, Consumer Discretionary, Financials, and Healthcare — all HOT with bullish MACD. Financials and Healthcare are running overbought (RSI 73 and 72). The validated Early-Runway signal has fired across Healthcare sub-industries (Health Information Services, Diagnostics & Research), which is where the validated funnel is concentrating today. Technology and Energy are the clear laggards; Energy's WTI RSI 28 washout may set up a mean-revert bounce but the trend remains down.

Forward watch: (1) does QQQ reclaim its 50-day and flip MACD positive — that would validate the sentiment narrative; (2) does the DXY strength persist and continue to cap gold/silver (validated inverse relationship); (3) does the Financials/Healthcare overbought reading resolve with a shallow pullback or a rotation exhaustion; (4) does VIX stay pinned below 20 to keep macro confidence at MEDIUM. Bull regime intact, but selective — hunt longs inside Early-Runway healthcare, not chase the tech narrative.

active.name: Geopolitical Risk Unwind — Iran Deal / Hormuz Reopening
active.thesis: The Iran nuclear deal and the Strait of Hormuz reopening have resolved near-term crude supply-disruption risk. WTI crude has fallen approximately 5% to near $80/barrel as the geopolitical risk premium unwinds. This is unambiguously RISK-ON for equities: lower crude reduces input-cost and inflation-expectation pressure, eases the case for further Fed tightening, and removes the dominant macro tail-risk from the narrative. The correct read on oil weakness here is NOT 'Iran re-escalation risk' — it is the OPPOSITE: the Hormuz corridor is reopening and supply constraints are lifting. Energy equities (XLE, E&P names) face near-term margin compression from lower realized prices, but the broader equity market benefits. Transports and consumer discretionary are direct fuel-cost beneficiaries.
active.evidence: WTI crude ~$80 (-~5% from recent highs); crude trajectory shifting from HOLDING_BULLISH toward FADING_BULLISH/bearish. Natural gas divergence intact (independent supply story — not demand-driven). Broad commodity complex already fading (DBC, USO, BNO).

Everything downstream this week hangs off the buck.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The regime is CHOPPY/TRANSITIONAL (confidence 6/10) but the macro plumbing is orderly, not stressed: VIX 16.4 in contango with VIX3M at 19.0, SPY +1.6% above its 50SMA, 10Y at 4.47% drifting lower on the 21d, 2s dragging up +1.5%. That's a curve steepening quietly while equities absorb dollar-driven commodity destruction. SPY RSI 56.6 is trending — no fade edge per our posture rule — and the metals complex being oversold on RSI (Silver 41, Gold 44.6) is NOT a mean-reversion setup while DXY holds its trend. Oil at RSI 28.6 is in a trend, not a bounce candidate — WTI oversold historically kept falling (edge -3.87%, hit 51%).

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Money is flowing into domestic-earners and rate-sensitives that benefit from a firm dollar and easing long end: XLV +10.3%, XLF +10.0%, XLI +6.9%, XLU +5.1%, IWM +4.2% on 21d. Breadth is broad — 81.8% of sectors above their 50SMAs, S&P 5d bullish breadth 46.6% vs bearish 25.1%. Rotation is INTO Consumer Electronics, Software - Infrastructure, and one unmapped bucket; the Precious Metals and Broad Commodity themes are explicitly FADING (GLD/SLV/GDX all accelerating bearish, DBC/DBA/WEAT flipped). XLY is the one soft spot at -0.1%, but its trajectory is HOLDING_BULLISH.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** The clearest ceiling is Semiconductors: HOT 13 months, +258% gain — the max on record — with a formal CEILING flag. That's exits-not-entries territory even though the trend is still up. In contrast, Software - Infrastructure (HOT 1 month, only +3%) and Internet Content & Information (HOT 1 month, -5%) are early-innings HOT spells with UP trends and ACCELERATING/HOLDING_BULLISH trajectories — that's where the runway sits. Internet Retail is HOLDING_BULLISH with a 21d +12.4%, still early in its choppy spell. No un-run coiling names cleared the filter today, so the setup is: rotate down the AI stack from extended Semis into earlier Software/Internet cohorts rather than chase the leaders.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** DXY 101.80 resistance is the tripwire. A break through it extends the metals/commodity pain and keeps the domestic-earner leadership intact; a rejection back below the 21d SMA cracks the spine and would let Gold/Silver stage a real bounce (though remember: 88% of washout lows get retested within 60 days, so any first bounce in metals is not the all-clear).
